title: Chapter 67 — Portfolio Expansion
intro: Growing your trade book beyond appliances into adjacent opportunities and adjacent markets.

sections.title: Category Expansion
sections.content:
Every trade account that buys appliances from you also needs related products: vent hoods, garbage disposals, water filtration, outdoor kitchens, and specialty items like wine fridges, ice makers, and beverage centers. These are natural portfolio expansions that increase your revenue per account without acquiring new accounts.

Start with what you already carry. If your store sells outdoor grills and the builder is doing projects with outdoor kitchens, you are leaving revenue on the table by not offering it. 'We also carry the outdoor kitchen line — want me to add it to your next spec?'

sections.title: Geographic Expansion
sections.content:
If your strongest builder accounts are expanding into new developments outside your core territory, follow them. The builder who trusts you in one market will use you in the next if you can deliver there.

Conversely, look at adjacent geographic markets where you have no trade presence. New developments, new subdivisions, new condo projects. Map them, identify the builders, and prospect. The same skills that built your current book apply to the next market.

sections.title: Service Expansion
sections.content:
Consider what services your trade accounts need beyond product supply: design consultation for their clients, specification support, project coordination, and warranty management. Each service deepens the relationship and increases switching costs.

The trade rep who provides products AND services is infrastructure. The one who only provides products is a vendor. Infrastructure is hard to displace. Vendors are easy to replace.
